basis: Paper's own comparison table shows cgroup-eBPF and KrakenGuard provide load-time admission control or partial isolation but neither combines enforced dispatch isolation with per-tenant state isolation the way vBPF does.

source_title: vBOIDs: Taming Chaos via Coarse-grained Scheduling Abstraction for Containers
basis: Paper's own evaluation shows vBOIDs matches or beats Firecracker's scheduling stability/throughput without hypervisor overhead, but explicitly trades away Firecracker's guest-kernel isolation.

source_title: Rethinking Process Snapshots for Near-Warm Serverless Cold Starts
target: REAP / FaaSnap (VM-boundary snapshot restore, cited baselines)
basis: Spice is evaluated head-to-head against these VM-boundary snapshot systems and attributes part of their overhead specifically to guest-OS virtual-clock-jump housekeeping, a VM-virtualization-specific cost a process-boundary mechanism avoids.

source_title: Rethinking Process Snapshots for Near-Warm Serverless Cold Starts
basis: Both operate at the process boundary; Spice replaces CRIU's syscall-replay reconstruction with a single kernel-level sparse-mapping primitive.

source_title: DVLA: Dynamic VM Lifetime Aware Scheduling for Drifting Lifetime Distributions a
basis: Both are VM placement/rescheduling papers that treat live migration as a budgeted operational primitive rather than a mechanism under study; VMR2L (EuroSys25) optimizes migration destination choice for CPU defragmentation, DVLA (OSDI26) optimizes initial+corrective placement by predicted VM lifetime -- complementary levers on the same VM-fleet-packing problem.

source_title: TelePod: Live Migration for Stateful Containers
target: VM pre-copy live migration (Clark et al., NSDI 2005)
basis: Abstract explicitly frames TelePod's technique as combining pre-copy iterative memory transfer (the classical hypervisor live-migration technique) with a new overlapped transmission-restoration step, and benchmarks against hypervisor-based VM migration performance.

source_title: TelePod: Live Migration for Stateful Containers
basis: Prototype is explicitly 'based on modified Checkpoint/Restore In Userspace (CRIU)'.

source_title: Priority-Aware GPU Co-Scheduling for High Performance Computing
basis: Both papers modify GPU resource-sharing behavior at the driver/scheduler layer (MPS priority vs. SVM migration/eviction) without introducing a new virtual-GPU abstraction, illustrating two different SUPPORT-level improvements to existing GPU virtualization/sharing mechanisms.

source_title: Enhanced SVM for Improving Application Performance Under GPU Memory Oversubscrip
basis: Both papers are SUPPORT-level improvements to existing GPU sharing/virtualization mechanisms (SVM paging policy vs. MPS scheduling policy) rather than new virtual-GPU abstractions.

source_title: Enabling Floating Point Virtualization With Tiny Numbers
target: Virtualization So Light, It Floats! Accelerating Floating Point Virtualization (Wanninger, Dhiantravan, Dinda; HPDC 2025, DOI 10.1145/3731545.3731584)
basis: Same senior/last author (Peter Dinda) and the same overall floating-point-virtualization research program (per the author's own publication list, listed consecutively as HPDC 2025 and HPDC 2026 entries); the 2025 system (FPVM) uses trap-and-emulate plus 'NaN-boxing' to virtualize toward LARGER alternative arithmetic (MPFR, posits, interval arithmetic), while the 2026 abstract explicitly targets th

source_title: Krysha: Cost-Efficient Resource Orchestration for Geo-Distributed Serverless Mic
basis: Both papers concern the mismatch between fixed VM/instance resource bundles and actual workload needs — one at the level of raw IaaS VM catalogs (CCGrid26-02), the other at the level of serverless function provisioning built atop those instances (this paper).

source_title: HD-IOV: SW-HW Co-designed I/O Virtualization with Scalability and Flexibility fo
basis: Both target SR-IOV's fixed-VF-count scaling ceiling for high-density multi-tenant hosts; HD-IOV's software-mediated, PASID/queue-pair-level isolation is a direct architectural predecessor to SG-IOV's socket-granular hardware partitioning for SmartNIC container networks.

source_title: Hoda: a High-performance Open vSwitch Dataplane with Multiple Specialized Data P
basis: Both are ByteDance-affiliated virtual-switch performance efforts a year apart (Hoda authors include ByteDance co-authors Peng He, Junjie Wan, Yuhao Zhou, Xiongchun Duan, Yu Zhang). Hoda keeps Open vSwitch but specializes its datapath per OpenFlow program; Byte vSwitch (2025) discards OVS entirely for a purpose-built forwarding engine - together they read as successive ByteDance strategies (patch-t

source_title: Orion: Interference-aware, Fine-grained GPU Sharing for ML Applications
basis: Orion achieves sharing purely in software at kernel granularity with no security isolation, the opposite trade-off point from hardware-partitioned MIG instances.

source_title: SmartNIC Security Isolation in the Cloud with S-NIC
basis: Both build mechanisms for safe SmartNIC multi-tenancy; OSMOSIS focuses on resource multiplexing/QoS across tenants while S-NIC focuses on hard hardware isolation against a distrusting host OS.

source_title: SmartNIC Security Isolation in the Cloud with S-NIC
basis: S-NIC's isolation model (locked TLBs, denylists, cache/bus partitioning) is exactly the class of accelerator-sharing protection that DSAssassin shows can be bypassed on a different shared accelerator (Intel DSA) via an unisolated Device TLB and shared work queue.

source_title: Pronghorn: Effective Checkpoint Orchestration for Serverless Hot-Starts
basis: Both optimize serverless cold/hot start via snapshot management (Pronghorn: which/when to checkpoint a CRIU process snapshot; Sabre: how to compress/restore a Firecracker microVM snapshot faster) at different layers of the isolation stack (process checkpoint vs. VM snapshot).

source_title: Sabre: Hardware-Accelerated Snapshot Compression for Serverless MicroVMs
basis: Both target serverless cold/hot-start cost via snapshot mechanisms, one at the VM layer (Sabre/Firecracker) and one at the process/CRIU layer (Pronghorn).

source_title: Managing Memory Tiers with CXL in Virtualized Environments
basis: Both concern tiered/CXL memory management; Nomad addresses OS-level page migration mechanics for a single host, while this paper adds the multi-tenant/VM isolation layer (page coloring) on top of a similar tiering substrate.

source_title: Microkernel Goes General: Performance and Compatibility in the HongMeng Producti
basis: Paper explicitly contrasts its OS-service isolation classes and shared-memory co-management with the 'double memory management'/'double thread scheduling' overhead and nested-page-table costs that hypervisor-based VM isolation incurs.

source_title: Burstable Cloud Block Storage with Data Processing Units
basis: Both are Alibaba/production-scale device-virtualization papers addressing per-tenant resource control at a DPU/IOMMU-mediated I/O boundary for passthrough-style VM storage/NIC access.

source_title: Nomad: Non-Exclusive Memory Tiering via Transactional Page Migration
basis: Nomad's transactional page migration is a host-OS-level tiering mechanism of the same kind that a hypervisor-level, multi-tenant tiering system (Managing Memory Tiers with CXL) would need to build on or extend for a VM setting.

source_title: ServerlessLLM: Low-Latency Serverless Inference for Large Language Models
basis: Both apply snapshot/checkpoint-loading and migration ideas from the VM/serverless world to speed up cold starts, one for Firecracker microVMs (Sabre) and one for LLM model checkpoints (ServerlessLLM).

source_title: vSoC: Efficient Virtual System-on-Chip on Heterogeneous Hardware
basis: vSoC explicitly breaks from the modular isolated-virtual-device architecture used on PC/server hardware because mobile SoCs are unified-memory, requiring a fundamentally different (shared-virtual-memory) device-virtualization design.

source_title: VPRI: Efficient I/O Page Fault Handling via Software-Hardware Co-Design for IaaS
basis: Both solve device-passthrough memory-safety/overcommit costs at the IOMMU/DMA boundary -- F&S cuts the cost of strict per-DMA IOTLB invalidation for a fixed pinned memory footprint, while VPRI removes the need for static pinning at all via software-managed IOPF; together they cover complementary corners of the passthrough safety/performance/memory-elasticity trade-off space.

source_title: Fast & Safe IO Memory Protection
basis: F&S makes strict per-DMA IOMMU protection cheap for a statically-pinned passthrough memory footprint, while VPRI removes the need for static pinning via software-managed IOPF; both attack the passthrough safety/performance/memory-cost triangle from different corners.

source_title: Unifying serverless and microservice workloads with SigmaOS
basis: Both are new OS-level isolation mechanisms (SigmaOS's sigma-containers vs. KFlex's kernel-extension safety split) built specifically to reduce the cost of an existing isolation boundary rather than to consume one.

source_title: PeRF: Preemption-enabled RDMA Framework
basis: Both virtualize a physical I/O device (RNIC vs SmartNIC) for multi-tenant performance isolation via software resource-multiplexing mechanisms rather than hardware SR-IOV partitioning.

source_title: OSMOSIS: Enabling Multi-Tenancy in Datacenter SmartNICs
basis: Both are software/hardware mechanisms that add multi-tenant performance isolation to a physical I/O device (RNIC vs SmartNIC) that natively lacks it.

source_title: A Secure, Fast, and Resource-Efficient Serverless Platform with Function REWIND
basis: Both attack cheap sandboxed-execution restart in serverless/microVM settings, but REWIND resets a container in place via CoW page-table bookkeeping while PASS/SnapStart restores a whole MicroVM from a persistent-memory snapshot.

source_title: Expeditious High-Concurrency MicroVM SnapStart in Persistent Memory with an Augm
basis: Both attack cheap sandboxed-execution restart in serverless/microVM settings, but REWIND resets a container in place via CoW page-table bookkeeping while PASS/SnapStart restores a whole MicroVM from a persistent-memory snapshot.

source_title: Taming Hot Bloat Under Virtualization with HugeScope
basis: Both operate on the hypervisor's EPT-mediated view of guest memory to improve VM memory-management decisions (HyperAlloc for de/inflation, HugeScope for hot/cold classification under huge pages).

source_title: On-demand and Parallel Checkpoint/Restore for GPU Applications
basis: Both use on-demand, page-fault-driven restoration to cut cold-start latency for accelerated/serverless workloads, one for whole MicroVMs (PASS) and one for GPU application state (gCROP).

source_title: KACE: Kernel-Aware Colocation for Efficient GPU Spatial Sharing
basis: Both address GPU sharing among concurrent workloads (KACE via MPS colocation of training/inference jobs, StreamBox via streams for serverless inference), illustrating different points on the spatial/temporal GPU-sharing spectrum.

source_title: Process-as-a-Service: Unifying Elastic and Stateful Clouds with Serverless Proce
basis: Both use a swap/serialize-to-storage lifecycle to cut cost while preserving state, but PASS/SnapStart snapshots a whole MicroVM's guest-physical memory at the hypervisor level while PraaS serializes one application process's state at the platform-API level.

source_title: SURE: Secure Unikernels Make Serverless Computing Rapid and Efficient
basis: Both are unikernel systems papers in the same SoCC 2024 session ('The Basics'); uIO focuses on making unikernels extensible/portable while SURE applies unikernels specifically to serverless isolation.

source_title: uIO: Lightweight and Extensible Unikernels
basis: Both build in-process isolation domains for untrusted/auxiliary code sharing an address space with a trusted body of code -- uIO uses x86 MPK (or eBPF) inside a unikernel guest, LightZone uses ARM64 TTBR/PAN switching for regular multi-threaded processes; alternative hardware primitives for the same isolation-domain-count/switch-cost trade-off.

source_title: uIO: Lightweight and Extensible Unikernels
basis: Both are unikernel-architecture papers in the same SoCC 2024 session; SURE applies Unikraft to serverless sandbox isolation while uIO makes Unikraft runtime-extensible without breaking its isolation model.

source_title: Securing a Multiprocessor KVM Hypervisor with Rust
target: HypSec / SeKVM (Arm KVM confidential hypervisor line)
basis: The paper directly implements and benchmarks against 'HypSec-5.15', a C-based implementation of the same EL2-Rcore/deprivileged-host design; KrustVM is a Rust re-implementation of that same architecture, aimed at eliminating memory-safety bugs in the C TCB.

source_title: Securing a Multiprocessor KVM Hypervisor with Rust
basis: Both address correctness/trust of a commodity hypervisor's TCB (one via a safe-language rewrite with compile-time guarantees, the other via testing); complementary approaches to the same hypervisor-correctness problem in taxonomy T7.

source_title: Towards Swap-Free, Continuous Ballooning for Fast, Cloud-Based Virtual Machine M
basis: HyperAlloc replaces virtio-balloon/virtio-mem with a shared page-frame allocator interface to make de/inflation fast and DMA-safe; this paper instead keeps the classic balloon-driver protocol but makes it safe to run continuously (including during migration) by adding real-time coordination logic -- two different fixes to the same 'ballooning is risky/slow' problem.

source_title: Towards Swap-Free, Continuous Ballooning for Fast, Cloud-Based Virtual Machine M
basis: Squeezy attacks slow VM memory reclamation for serverless FaaS VMs by making the guest kernel aware of hotplugged-vs-ordinary memory; this paper attacks the safety (OOM/swap) of ballooning-based deflation for live-migrated cloud VMs -- both are 2024-2026 responses to the same underlying VM-memory-elasticity design space the brief highlights as a lineage (HyperAlloc/Squeezy).

source_title: PCLive: Pipelined Restoration of Application Containers for Reduced Service Down
basis: PCLive is implemented as a modification to CRIU and runC, restructuring CRIU's restore path from a single-shot operation into a pipelined, dependency-ordered one.

source_title: Faascale: Scaling MicroVM Vertically for Serverless Computing with Memory Elasti
basis: HyperAlloc gives full KVM VMs fast, DMA-safe memory de/inflation via a hypervisor-shared page-frame allocator; Faascale applies the same 'runtime VM memory elasticity' goal to Firecracker microVMs via a coordinated guest+VMM+host-kernel path -- same taxonomy branch (T2), different VM weight class.

source_title: Faascale: Scaling MicroVM Vertically for Serverless Computing with Memory Elasti
basis: Squeezy makes reclamation of hotplugged VM memory fast for serverless FaaS VMs by making the guest kernel hotplug-aware; Faascale's guest+host-kernel-coordinated vertical scaling for Firecracker microVMs targets the same serverless-VM-memory-elasticity problem from the microVM side of the design space.

source_title: Snapipeline: Accelerating Snapshot Startup for FaaS Containers
basis: Both titles indicate pipelined restoration/snapshot-startup mechanisms for containerized workloads in the same SoCC 2024 'Speed and Scale in Serverless' / 'Elastic Cloud' session cluster; grouped for the same restore-pipelining design question.

source_title: Direct Memory Translation for Virtualized Clouds
target: EPT/NPT nested paging (Intel/AMD hardware 2D page walk)
basis: Paper positions DMT/pvDMT as replacing the sequential 2D EPT/NPT walk with a single direct-mapped reference.

source_title: Verifying Rust Implementation of Page Tables in a Software Enclave Hypervisor
target: Extended Page Tables / SGX-style enclave isolation
basis: HyperEnclave is a software TEE that virtualizes enclave memory via EPTs analogous to SGX/EPT hardware isolation.

source_title: GMLake: Efficient and Transparent GPU Memory Defragmentation for Large-scale DNN
basis: Both papers apply virtual-memory decoupling/remapping (VMA-to-physical for CPU/VMs, GPU virtual-to-physical for DNN training) to eliminate a translation/fragmentation bottleneck.

source_title: Lightweight Fault Isolation: Practical, Efficient, and Secure Software Sandboxin
basis: Paper directly benchmarks LFI against WAMR/wasm2c as competing lightweight-isolation mechanisms for untrusted code.

source_title: RainbowCake: Mitigating Cold-starts in Serverless with Layer-wise Container Cach
basis: Both target serverless cold-start/idle-container memory cost in the same 'Serverless Computing 1' ASPLOS 2024 session, from complementary angles (container-cache layering vs container memory offloading).

source_title: FaaSMem: Improving Memory Efficiency of Serverless Computing with Memory Pool Ar
basis: Both address the cost of keeping serverless containers warm; FaaSMem attacks memory footprint, RainbowCake attacks cache-layer duplication.

source_title: RAP: Resource-aware Automated GPU Sharing for Multi-GPU Recommendation Model Tra
basis: RAP explicitly benchmarks against and avoids relying on MIG/MPS hardware partitioning, instead using a software cost model.

source_title: Pentimento: Data Remanence in Cloud FPGAs
target: Cloud FPGA multi-tenancy providers' logical-wipe isolation model
basis: Paper demonstrates the providers' stated isolation guarantee (logical scrub between tenants) is insufficient against a physical side channel.

source_title: Last-Level Cache Side-Channel Attacks Are Feasible in the Modern Public Cloud
basis: Both are ASPLOS 2024 attacks demonstrating that public-cloud multi-tenancy isolation (co-location, cache sharing) is weaker in practice than platform abstractions suggest.

source_title: Everywhere All at Once: Co-Location Attacks on Public Cloud FaaS
basis: Companion paper by the same authors; this establishes co-location, the other exploits it via LLC side channel.

source_title: Loupe: Driving the Development of OS Compatibility Layers
basis: Loupe's headline case study retroactively analyzes OSv's Linux compatibility layer and shows it over-implemented syscalls relative to what its supported apps need.

source_title: TrackFM: Far-out Compiler Support for a Far Memory World
basis: Both concern memory-address handling for remote/virtualized resources, but TrackFM stays at compiler-instrumentation level with no new virtual-memory abstraction, unlike DMT's hardware-register-based translation layer.

source_title: ParvaGPU: Efficient Spatial GPU Sharing for Large-Scale DNN Inference in Cloud E
target: NVIDIA Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) and Multi-Process Service (MPS)
basis: Paper explicitly builds its scheduler on top of these two existing NVIDIA GPU-sharing technologies rather than replacing them.

source_title: Efficient Tensor Offloading for Large Deep-Learning Model Training based on Comp
basis: Extends CXL cache-coherence to accelerator-CPU tensor offload, a specific instance of the broader CXL memory-virtualization design space.

source_title: ESG: Pipeline-Conscious Efficient Scheduling of DNN Workflows on Serverless Plat
basis: Both schedule serverless/inference workloads over NVIDIA MIG vGPU partitions rather than building a new GPU virtualization mechanism.

source_title: DataStates-LLM: Lazy Asynchronous Checkpointing for Large Language Models
basis: Both must move large, mutable-during-execution state asynchronously without stopping the workload; DataStates-LLM does this for training state instead of VM/container images.

source_title: vPIM: Processing-in-Memory Virtualization
basis: Uses the same guest-frontend / VMM-backend virtio queue pattern as paravirtualized NIC/block device virtualization.

source_title: Guardian: Safe GPU Sharing in Multi-Tenant Environments
target: NVIDIA MIG / MPS (hardware or driver-enforced GPU partitioning)
basis: Both address unsafe GPU sharing, but Guardian achieves it in software (PTX instrumentation) with measured 4-12% overhead instead of hardware-partitioned isolation.

source_title: Menos: Split Fine-Tuning Large Language Models with Efficient GPU Memory Sharing
basis: Both are GPU spatial/temporal sharing mechanisms presented at the same Middleware 2024 GPU session, addressing memory-safety (Guardian) and memory-capacity (Menos) sides of GPU multi-tenancy respectively.

source_title: Near-Storage Processing in FaaS Environments with Funclets
basis: Funclets is built directly on the Faasm WebAssembly multi-tenant FaaS runtime and its existing sandboxing/threading model.

source_title: Privagic: automatic code partitioning with explicit secure typing
basis: Privagic's partitioned output places sensitive code/data inside an SGX enclave; SGX itself is the trusted-execution mechanism it builds on.

source_title: LightZone: Lightweight Hardware-Assisted In-Process Isolation for ARM64
basis: uIO uses x86 Memory Protection Keys (plus an eBPF software fallback) to isolate an in-unikernel auxiliary-code context sharing the guest's address space; LightZone uses ARM64 TTBR/PAN switching to isolate domains within an ordinary multi-threaded process -- alternative hardware primitives for the same in-process-isolation-domain problem, on different ISAs and host environments.

source_title: LightZone: Lightweight Hardware-Assisted In-Process Isolation for ARM64
target: Intel MPK / VMFUNC-based in-process isolation (e.g. sMVX)
basis: The paper explicitly frames ARM64 as lacking a native equivalent to Intel VMFUNC/MPK and designs TTBR+PAN switching to fill that gap; a direct cross-ISA contrast for the same isolation-domain-count/switch-cost design point.

source_title: Tackling Memory Footprint Expansion During Live Migration of Virtual Machines
basis: Both papers, by the same Binghamton group, address sharing-awareness in live migration; VIRT-CCGRID24-03 is the Doctoral Symposium presentation of directly-related work on multi-VM live migration memory sharing.

source_title: Incorporating Memory Sharing-awareness in Multi-VM Live Migration
basis: Explicitly generalizes the single-VM sharing-aware live migration mechanism to the multi-VM migration setting, per title and shared authorship.

source_title: IvLeague: Side Channel-resistant Secure Architectures Using Isolated Domains of
basis: Both fix a shared/central management or metadata structure (EMS mailbox vs integrity-tree) that leaks information across otherwise-isolated enclave/TEE domains on the same physical processor.

source_title: IvLeague: Side Channel-resistant Secure Architectures Using Isolated Domains of
basis: Both extend SGX-class enclave isolation with a new structural mechanism (data enclaves vs TreeLings) addressing a limitation of the stock SGX integrity/sharing model.

source_title: Veiled Pathways: Investigating Covert and Side Channels Within GPU Uncore
basis: STAR improves a shared GPU structure (L3 TLB) within MIG's isolation model for performance; Veiled Pathways shows other shared, unpartitioned GPU uncore structures (PCIe, codec engines, DRAM frequency control) break that same isolation model for security -- two views of what MIG does and does not actually partition.

source_title: Mosaic: Harnessing the Micro-Architectural Resources of Servers in Serverless En
basis: Both partition a normally-shared microarchitectural structure (L3 TLB for MIG GPU instances; L2/LLC/TLB/BTB for serverless functions) to give genuine per-tenant isolation/state retention within an existing multi-tenancy model.
